161.context: After drinks, familiar music draws the swordswoman into an admired dance. Hodram recognizes another side of her and compliments it. Keep the affectionate surprise; the final reference to ミヴォール conveys admiration without establishing an unspoken romantic relationship.
notes: The numbered customers are explicit FE body headings, not native actor nameplates.
Do not turn 惚れ込む into a new spouse, lover or courtship fact without linked source support.
meanings: Hodram remarks that he has drunk quite a lot for the first time in a while.
His companion agrees that she has had plenty too, then notices something.
Hodram appreciates the music.
She recognizes this piece and excuses herself briefly.
Hodram acknowledges her.
Under the Customer 1 heading, a spectator exclaims about the impressive woman.
Under Customer 2, another admires both her beauty and her dancing.
Hodram watches silently.
Both customer headings accompany an enthusiastic chorus of Bravo.
Applause is heard or represented.
She says she could not resist dancing because she loves this piece.
Hodram had thought swordsmanship was her sole pursuit or talent.
She asks whether he was surprised.
He admits it, praises the dance and says he understands why ミヴォール is so taken with her.

162.context: A persistent street seller wants to travel. Hodram's stern refusal meets cheeky replies, then a cooking sample wins him over despite the applicant declaring acceptance prematurely. Preserve playful persistence and the tacit concession rather than a formal earlier hiring decision.
notes: Elephants and heat do not by themselves identify a country or nationality.
ガキ is Hodram's dismissive address; do not invent an exact age or make the narrator classify the applicant as a child.
The applicant says he has no shipboard experience, not that he has no useful abilities.
meanings: Hodram comments on the considerable heat.
A seller energetically advertises good merchandise to passersby.
Notices unusual customers and asks whether they are travelers.
Asks to go along: he is tired of seeing elephants and wants to visit other countries.
Hodram asks his special skill.
Proudly says he is good at cooking.
Hodram asks about experience aboard ship.
The applicant cheerfully admits he has none.
Hodram says he cannot rely on someone like that.
The applicant points out that everyone has a first time.
Hodram also rejects people who talk back.
The applicant doubts that this reply counts as talking back.
Hodram insists he has no use for a troublesome brat.
The applicant retorts that Hodram was a brat himself not long ago.
Hodram reacts sharply.
The applicant declares he dislikes Hodram and says goodbye.
Hodram calls him strange and proposes returning to the ship.
The applicant runs after him, asks him to wait and retracts his insult: he likes him after all.
Hodram says nothing.
The applicant offers his own cooking and proposes being judged after a taste.
Hodram agrees that trying some food is harmless, then tastes it.
He reacts with impressed surprise.
The applicant anxiously asks how it is and whether he is still rejected.
Hodram pauses without stating a decision.
The applicant reads approval in his face and celebrates.
Hodram points out that he has not said anything yet.
Introduces himself as Samwell and boasts that he is handy enough to do anything.
Hodram finds him exasperating.
Privately concedes that the food is excellent.

163.context: A missing ship causes alarm and exaggerated scientific disbelief. The port witness eventually explains that one lanky man sailed away alone. Keep the comic shift from an apparent disappearance to an unauthorized departure; do not invent magic, disappearance of the entire fleet or witnessed theft details beyond the report.
meanings: A crew member urgently reports to the admiral that the ship is gone.
Hodram repeats the report incredulously.
Gerhard cannot believe a ship could simply disappear.
Charles declares it scientifically and physically impossible.
The crew member insists it is true and asks him to come immediately to the departure office.
Hodram reacts in shock.
The crew member anxiously asks what to do.
Gerhard is astonished that it has vanished without a trace.
Charles cannot explain it scientifically and finds it baffling.
Someone at the port calls to the admiral.
Reports seeing a lanky young man working on the ship alone early that morning.
Then the man sailed away.
Gerhard demands why the witness watched without stopping him.
Charles comments mildly that this is a troublesome situation.
The witness never expected him to depart: being alone, he seemed merely to be inspecting the ship.
Hodram finds the culprit remarkably bold for sailing out alone.
Gerhard proposes returning to town, gathering information and finding the man.

164.context: A short port update while awaiting the unauthorized sailor's return; keep it consistent with the adjacent duplicate variant without inventing a new event.
meanings: The port speaker says the man or ship apparently has not returned yet.

165.context: A second source occurrence of the same waiting update; preserve its independent exact reference and do not double-count it as the same stored record.
meanings: The port speaker says the man or ship apparently has not returned yet.

166.context: The missing ship returns with Jam, whose absurd found-ship explanation and improvised maxims infuriate Gerhard but amuse Hodram. A deliberately abrupt false refusal becomes acceptance. Preserve the flamboyant voice, exact J-A-M spelling, two-second joke, invented proverb and the contrast with prudent long living.
notes: Do not validate the abandoned-ship claim as a narrator fact; it is Jam's excuse.
人生是極太激短 is deliberately made up, as Hodram's aside confirms; a stock proverb can erase the joke.
Full-name Latin spelling must be bound to the approved native names before localized drafting; retain ジャム・ジャック・ルドワイヤン as the clean reference.
meanings: The port speaker excitedly reports that the ship has returned.
Hodram reacts in surprise.
The witness points out the unmistakable ship.
The returning man exuberantly celebrates the vast, wonderful sea.
He has enjoyed himself since morning and declares it another refreshing day.
Hodram chuckles at the variety of people in the world.
Gerhard demands whose permission allowed him aboard.
The man claims the ship was simply lying around.
Gerhard objects incredulously.
Charles declares a ship lying around at sea scientifically impossible.
The man insists he found it while walking by the port, looking lonely and abandoned.
Claims kindhearted Jam picked it up; explicitly spells his name J-A-M and cheers.
Hodram infers that he also decided to try sailing it, but asks how he managed to move it.
He vaguely describes doing this and that and somehow making it work.
Hodram is impressed despite himself.
Charles says it would ordinarily be impossible and risks shipwreck or running aground.
The man dismisses that concern and announces a maxim they should listen to.
Quotes the idea that trying makes achievement possible and decides that his personal approval makes it fine.
Another crew member comments that an alarming eccentric has appeared.
Hodram chuckles.
Gerhard demands that he stop treating this as a joke.
Jam declares everything acceptable because he is himself and coins a pseudo-proverb about an intensely full but extremely short life.
Hodram privately notes that no such proverb exists.
Jam rejects timid, small-scale living for the sake of a long life as unbearably dull.
Gerhard, exasperated, proposes handing him to the guards.
Hodram says he likes him.
Gerhard asks in disbelief whether he is sane.
Hodram is serious: sailing alone and those reckless convictions make him unusually interesting.
Gerhard begins to suspect the next proposal.
Charles fears that Hodram might mean to recruit him.
Hodram confirms it, checks that the name was Jam and asks him to come along.
Jam theatrically weighs the offer, borrows Just a moment and asks for precisely two seconds to think.
He announces a decision.
Hodram asks whether he has decided.
Jam says yes: he will not go, bids them farewell and wishes them a good voyage.
Hodram falls silent.
Jam complains about the small reaction, tells him not to be angry and reveals the refusal was a joke.
Hodram questions whether it was a joke.
Jam really wants to join; formally reintroduces himself as ジャム・ジャック・ルドワイヤン and cheers.
